newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt soars as U.S. payrolls lift bond hopes.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt soars as U.S. payrolls lift bond hopes.

text.p: Emerging debt prices soared Thursday when a tame report on U.S. job growth spurred prospects for global bond markets, traders said.

The U.S. Treasury market led the surge after the U.S. Labor Department reported non-farm payrolls rose by 217,000 jobs, fewer than market expectations, while the unemployment rate rose to 5.0 percent.

The data fueled optimism for emerging debt, as players revelled in the prospect that moderate non-inflationary U.S. growth might convince the Federal Reserve to stick to its gradual approach to tighening U.S. interest rates.
"Everyone wants to buy bonds," one Brady bond trader said. "Treasuries look good, stocks look good. It's a holiday and it's summer. People are happy and they're long."
Emerging debt trade ended at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT Thursday ahead of Friday's U.S. Independence Day holiday.
The trader reported seeing client interest in Venezuelan, Peruvian and Russian paper, as investors loaded up on assets for the second quarter.
"More money continues to come into the market," said Gary Evans, global debt strategist at UBS Securities. "Investors are moving down the credit curve and reallocating to the emerging markets."
Fixed rate instruments and high yield Bradies led the more liquid market floaters, based on the strength of the U.S. bond market, traders said.
"It's definitely Treasury led," the head Brady trader at one U.S. investment bank said. "The floaters aren't doing so well. I think everybody is going for the fixed trade long stuff today."
Late Thursday, the benchmark 30-year U.S. T-bond gained 1-7/32 to yield 6.62 percent.
Of the most liquid Latin American instruments, Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR rose 1-1/8 to 82-3/8, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR lagged behind, gaining 1/8 to 94-1/2.
"We've seen a fair amount buying in Russia, Mexico, and a little bit in Venezuela," one trader said.
Mexico's global bond due 2026 MXUMS=RR gained 7/8 to 116-7/8, while its par bonds MX625L19=RR rose 1-1/8 to 79-5/8.

Mexican paper prospered ahead of Sunday's key congressional election, even though polls showed the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may lose its lower house majority for the first time since 1929.
U.S. investors said shrugged off political uncertainties in Mexico because of the resilient Mexican economy, which was forecast to grow at more than five percent this year.
